title: Free Boho Nursery Printable Wall Art
excerpt: Skip the boutique prices. This free boho nursery wall art printable comes in warm terracotta, sage, and cream tones, sized for standard frames, so you can finish the nursery for the cost of a sheet of paper.
quick_answer: Boho nursery wall art is soft, earthy decor featuring rainbows, arches, suns, moons, and botanical line art in warm terracotta, sage, and cream tones. Get it free by downloading a print-ready PDF, printing it on matte paper at home, and framing it for a coordinated nursery gallery wall on any budget.

faq_items.question: Where can I find free boho nursery wall art to print?
faq_items.answer: You can download free boho nursery wall art as high-resolution PDF files and print them at home or at a copy shop. Look for files built at 300 DPI and sized to standard frames, like the boho rainbow print here, so they come out crisp and frame-worthy instead of blurry on paper.

faq_items.question: What colors work best in a boho nursery?
faq_items.answer: A warm, muted palette works best: a neutral base of cream and oatmeal with terracotta, sage green, and dusty blush accents. Keep saturation low so the room feels calm rather than loud. The palette is gender-neutral and grows well into a toddler room later without a full redo.

faq_items.question: What size should I print nursery wall art?
faq_items.answer: Most boho nursery printables are sized for standard 8x10 and 5x7 frames, which suit gallery walls and shelf ledges. Print those at home on matte paper, and send larger focal sizes like 11x14 or 16x20 to a pharmacy or print shop on matte poster stock for a few dollars.

faq_items.question: Is it safe to hang framed art over a crib?
faq_items.answer: No. Never hang framed art or anything heavy directly over where the baby sleeps. Place prints on the wall above the dresser, on a shelf, or to the side of the crib instead, and secure frames well. This keeps the boho look while keeping the sleep space safe.

faq_items.question: How do I arrange a boho nursery gallery wall?
faq_items.answer: Start with an odd number of prints and one larger anchor, like a boho rainbow, then build outward. Keep a shared warm palette, lay everything on the floor first to test spacing (about 2 to 3 inches between frames), and mix natural wood, rattan, and off-white frames for a collected look.
